answer: Approval cannot be given on the facts supplied. The existing silica cable transmits only about 350-2400 nm, so it cannot carry the mid-infrared ATR signal used for water in petroleum, and mid-IR reach over a link to another building is not documented. Test MIR ATR for water in petroleum in the laboratory first, then confirm a mid-IR fiber link with AFS.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR for water in petroleum in the laboratory before any in-line install
inline.probe: ZrO2 ATR probe sealed in PEEK shaft with PEEK tubing, as in the published water-in-petroleum application
inline.install: Laboratory bench first; in-line at the petroleum line only after a mid-IR fiber link of the required length is confirmed
inline.fiber: Mid-IR fiber family: PIR (3-17 um) or CIR (1.1-6.5 um), which cover the 4000-2000 cm-1 (about 2.5-5 um) range; not the existing Vis-NIR silica cable
inline.test_against: NIR fiber probe on the existing silica cable, as a comparison only
inline.not_final_because: The silica cable cannot carry MIR, the link length and routing are unknown, mid-IR reach over distance is not documented, and no detection limit or process conditions are given.

problems.text: The existing silica cable transmits only about 350-2400 nm, so it cannot carry the mid-infrared signal needed for MIR ATR, which lies around 4000-2000 cm-1 (about 2.5-5 um). The cable cannot be reused for this method.

The sources give no reach for mid-IR fiber links. The 100-300 m figure applies only to low-OH silica for visible/NIR, so whether a mid-IR link to another building is feasible must be confirmed by AFS.
Approval needs the fiber type, link length, routing and operating conditions, and none of these has been supplied; the choice of method depends on them.

The water-in-petroleum example is a laboratory result. It shows absorbance rising with water from 0.1 to 2.0 %, but it gives no detection limit, link length or process conditions, so it does not show the method works on this line.

methods.why: The published water-in-petroleum application uses MIR ATR, and MIR gives well-defined absorption peaks suited to ATR contact with liquids.
NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and works with ordinary glass optics, so it could run on the existing silica cable; its response to water in petroleum is not shown in the sources.
Raman is complementary to MIR but needs special probes, and fluorescence of many organic compounds can mask its signal.
Its strongly overlapping signals complicate analysis of real mixtures, and the sources give no basis for water in petroleum.

experiment.objective: Show in the laboratory whether MIR ATR sees water in petroleum over the client's range before any link is approved.
steps: Prepare petroleum samples with a water series across the client's range; the published example uses 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 % water.
Record MIR ATR spectra over 4000-2000 cm-1 with a ZrO2 ATR probe in a PEEK shaft.
Send the same samples to an independent laboratory for water analysis as the reference values.
Build a chemometric model and validate it on samples held out from calibration.
Have AFS confirm mid-IR fiber reach (PIR or CIR) for the stated link length, and compare with the silica cable on NIR only as a reference.
references: S02 p.13: water in petroleum application example
S01 p.5-6: method comparison and Table 1
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the required accuracy and detection limit must be met on validation samples, and AFS must confirm mid-IR reach for the stated link length.

pathway.key_features: Absorbance across 4000-2000 cm-1 rises with water content in the application chart.
pathway.path_reason: Approval and mid-IR link feasibility are unresolved, so lab results are needed first.

multispectral.why: Fluorescence would add a different signal, but most chemicals do not fluoresce and no fluorescent component of petroleum is shown in the sources; the single method is not yet tested.
multispectral.test: Only if MIR ATR alone fails: compare MIR ATR alone with MIR ATR plus fluorescence on the same validation samples; the combination must beat MIR ATR alone.

assumptions: The petroleum line sample is a liquid that can make ATR contact.
The analyzer is far from the line; the distance is treated as unknown and beyond the silica cable's documented reach.
No water range, detection limit or process conditions have been given.
